decisions.description: Withdrawals are capped at a daily limit of 5000 per account, a value the plan never mentions.
The daily limit allows a withdrawal that brings the total to exactly 5000 (strict greater-than check).
The daily withdrawal counter is never reset, so the 'daily' limit is in fact a lifetime limit for the ledger instance.
The withdrawal limit is tracked per account rather than per customer or globally.
Transfers are not counted against the daily withdrawal limit, so funds can leave an account without limit via transfer.
Amounts are rounded to two decimal places using Math.round (half-up toward positive infinity, subject to floating-point error).
The positive-amount check happens before rounding, so an amount such as 0.001 is accepted, rounds to 0, and records a zero-value entry.
The positive-amount check accepts Infinity as a valid amount.
Balances are kept as floating-point numbers and are not re-rounded after arithmetic, so cents drift can accumulate.
Overdrafts are forbidden: withdrawals and transfers that would take the balance below zero are rejected as insufficient-funds.
A repeated transaction id returns success without checking that the account, amount or operation type match the original.
Transaction ids are deduplicated in one global namespace shared across all accounts and operation kinds.
Transaction ids are remembered only for accepted operations, so a rejected id can be reused and later succeed.
Amount validation runs before the duplicate check, so a retry with an invalid amount is rejected rather than acknowledged.
Seen transaction ids are kept forever with no expiry window.
Accounts are created implicitly on first use by any operation, including a withdrawal or transfer that is then rejected.
Querying the balance of an unknown account returns 0 instead of an error.
Querying the history of an unknown account returns an empty list instead of an error.
Failures are reported as result objects with fixed reason strings rather than thrown errors.
In a withdrawal the insufficient-funds check runs before the daily-limit check, deciding which reason is reported when both apply.
A transfer is recorded as two history entries sharing the same transaction id, transfer-out on the source then transfer-in on the destination.
History entries store only id, kind and rounded amount, with no timestamp, counterparty or resulting balance.
Account names and transaction ids are not validated, so empty or missing strings are accepted.
